stories.title: PGIM Sells Delray Beach Assisted Living Community for at Least $140M
stories.excerpt: PGIM Real Estate sold a relatively new assisted living facility in Delray Beach, Fla., for at least $140 million, marking one of the biggest South Florida retirement home sales in recent years. Chevy Chase, Md.-based Artemis Real Estate Partners purchased the 7.2-acre asset, property records show. The 224,951-square-foot community, called The Arbor at Delray, houses 207 apartments at 6595 Morikami Park Road, just west of South Jog Road. The complex includes a 35,586-square-foot recreational clubhouse and a 51,461-square-foot nursing home. The sale breaks down to just under $676,300 per unit, though it’s unclear whether the $140 million figure listed on the deed also includes the operations for the business, which could boost the price tag. PGIM Real Estate, part of insurance giant Prudential Financial, completed the property in 2023. Two years earlier, PGIM-backed Alliance Residential Company purchased the land for $8.2 million and secured a $45.7 million construction loan from Dallas-based Comerica Bank, The Real Deal reported. There’s been an uptick in the number of assisted living facilities across Palm Beach County this year as the occupancy rate in Florida neared 90 percent, with monthly rents averaging over $5,000 in the second quarter of 2026, according to data from Colliers. Just last week, Healthpeak Properties bought a 136-unit facility in Boynton Beach for at least $62 million. Representatives for Artemis and PGIM did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: PGIM Real Estate sold 207-unit Delray Beach assisted living facility for $140M+ in 2025.
Artemis Real Estate Partners acquired The Arbor at Delray; $676K per unit implies strong healthcare RE appetite.
PGIM built property in 2023; land purchased 2023 for $8.2M, construction loan $45.7M from Comerica.
stories.summary: PGIM Real Estate divested The Arbor at Delray, a 224,951-square-foot assisted living community with 207 units, to Artemis Real Estate Partners for at least $140 million. The property, completed in 2023, generated roughly $676,300 per unit and included a 35,586-square-foot clubhouse and 51,461-square-foot nursing home. PGIM had acquired the land for $8.2 million in 2021 and secured $45.7 million in construction financing from Comerica Bank.
stories.impact: Strong exit multiple on recent completion signals robust institutional capital appetite for senior housing in South Florida, despite higher cap rates. Successful monetization of this scale may encourage other operators to develop similar communities in Miami/Fort Lauderdale submarkets where demand remains strong from retiree in-migration, though construction costs and labor remain elevated barriers.

stories.title: Mamdani Invests $8.4M in Business Improvement Districts Citywide
stories.excerpt: Mayor Zohran Mamdani is upping the grant funding available to local organizations that promote commerce — though it doesn’t look like much. Mamdani and the New York City Department of Small Business Services (SBS) is making $8.4 million available to business improvement districts for public art displays, street cleaning, lighting and directories. While $8.4 million might not be the most impressive figure, the administration says it could boost foot traffic for 20,000 businesses in the five boroughs, and is the largest single cash infusion of its kind. “Our administration knows it’s not enough to make it easier to open a small business, you have to make it easier to visit one, too,” Mamdani said in a statement. “That’s why our commitment to small businesses means not only cutting red tape and reducing fines, but investing in the neighborhoods surrounding bodegas, bookshops and restaurants so that New York City is lined with ‘OPEN’ signs year-round.” The grant money has already been awarded, with Brooklyn taking the majority of available funding, or $2.7 million for 32 organizations, while 17 entities in the Bronx received $1.55 million, according to the administration. Manhattan and Queens received similar amounts, while the Bronx saw less funding and Staten Island got the least: $550,000 to only seven organizations. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: NYC Mayor Mamdani allocates $8.4M to business improvement districts across five boroughs.
Grants fund street cleaning, lighting, public art; intended to boost foot traffic for 20,000 businesses.
Brooklyn receives largest share; largest single NYC cash infusion for BIDs on record.
stories.summary: New York City's Department of Small Business Services, under Mayor Zohran Mamdani, awarded $8.4 million in grant funding to business improvement districts citywide for public art, street cleaning, lighting, and directories. The administration claims the investment could drive foot traffic to 20,000 small businesses across the five boroughs and represents the largest single cash infusion of its kind. Brooklyn received the plurality of funds.
stories.impact: Modest but signals municipal intent to support street-level retail vitality in walkable neighborhoods; marginal impact on multifamily demand itself, but sustained deterioration of local commercial districts (storefronts, street quality) can suppress renter foot-traffic and reduce lease-up velocity. Investment in BIDs may stabilize older urban submarkets and make transit-oriented multifamily development more attractive to capital.

stories.title: MBA: Multifamily Mortgage Volume Rose 32% in 2025
stories.excerpt: In 2025, 2,530 different multifamily lenders originated a total of $381.8 billion in new mortgages for multifamily properties with five or more units, according to the Mortgage Bankers Association’s (MBA) annual report of the multifamily lending market. The total represents a 32% increase over 2024 levels. “Multifamily lending gained significant momentum in 2025, with dollar volume increasing 32% from 2024 as lenders of all sizes remained active across a broad range of capital sources,” said Reggie Booker, MBA’s associate VP of commercial research. “Greater rate stability and clearer pricing expectations helped bring borrowers and lenders back to the market, supporting increased refinancing and acquisition activity throughout the year.” By dollar volume, the greatest share (40% of the total) went to GSEs Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac. The top five multifamily lenders in 2025 by dollar volume were JPMorgan Chase & Co., Wells Fargo, Walker & Dunlop, Berkadia and CBRE. The post MBA: Multifamily Mortgage Volume Rose 32% in 2025 appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Multifamily mortgage volume rose 32% YoY in 2025 to $381.8B across 2,530 lenders.
GSEs (Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac) captured 40% by dollar volume; JPMorgan Chase, Wells Fargo led top five.
Rate stability and clearer pricing expectations drove increased refinancing and acquisition activity.
stories.summary: The Mortgage Bankers Association reported multifamily mortgage originations totaled $381.8 billion in 2025, a 32% increase over 2024, across 2,530 lenders. GSEs underwrote 40% of total volume, with JPMorgan Chase, Wells Fargo, Walker & Dunlop, Berkadia, and CBRE rounding out the top five. The spike was attributed to greater rate stability and improved pricing visibility that brought borrowers and lenders back to market for refinancing and acquisitions.
stories.impact: Sharp rebound in multifamily lending capital availability and volume de-risks new development underwriting and refinance assumptions; stable rates and normalized spread pricing enable developers to lock construction and bridge loans at predictable costs. Indicates SOFR and rate uncertainty have largely cleared—a green light for pipeline acceleration and new starts throughout 2025–2026, especially in supply-constrained markets where acquisition and replacement of aging stock are economically justified.

stories.title: Common Group Unveils Goodyear Retail Center Plans
stories.excerpt: Common Bond Development Group revealed details for its latest commercial development: a premium, grocery-anchored shopping center in the master-planned community of Estrella in Goodyear, Arizona. The project brings together the City of Goodyear, developer Harvard Investments, and anchor tenant Sprouts Farmers Market to establish a new commercial heart for the trade area. Phase one of the development will total approximately 35,224 square feet, featuring a 23,024-square-foot Sprouts Farmers Market, 9,200 square feet of inline retail space, and a 3,000-square-foot standalone pad. A future second phase, situated along the lake, is planned to add 16,000 to 20,000 square feet of retail and restaurant space. The center’s initial design, completed by Suite 6 Architecture + Planning incorporates a maritime theme that reflects its location on Estrella Parkway at North Lake near the Yacht Club of Estrella and the Starpointe Residents’ Club. The project is targeted to break ground in the first quarter of 2027. The post Common Group Unveils Goodyear Retail Center Plans appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Common Bond Development Group launching grocery-anchored retail center in master-planned Estrella community, Goodyear, Arizona.
Phase one: 35,224 SF including 23,024 SF Sprouts Farmers Market, 9.2K SF inline retail, 3K SF pad.
Groundbreaking targeted Q1 2027; future phase two adds 16K–20K SF retail and restaurant along lake.
stories.summary: Common Bond Development Group, Harvard Investments, and anchor tenant Sprouts Farmers Market are developing a grocery-anchored shopping center in Goodyear, Arizona's master-planned Estrella community. Phase one comprises 35,224 square feet with Sprouts as anchor, inline retail, and a standalone pad, targeted to break ground in Q1 2027. A future lake-fronting phase two will add 16,000 to 20,000 square feet of retail and restaurant uses.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily relevance, but Estrella is a fast-growing master-planned community attracting younger families and working-age renters; strong retail/commercial anchoring in the trade area signals developer confidence in demographic trajectory and purchasing power. Retail success here may inform site selection for multifamily within or near Estrella, as new commercial nodes reduce car-dependence and increase local amenity appeal—key factors for lease-up velocity in Phoenix's sprawling suburban markets.

stories.title: Developer Plans 297 Housing Units Across From Downtown Brooklyn Macy’s Project
stories.excerpt: Another residential tower might be coming to Downtown Brooklyn, directly across from a major retail makeover project at the former Macy’s. Local developer Shimon Klein has filed plans with the New York City Department of Buildings to bring a trio of 99-unit residential buildings along Fulton Street between Bridge and Lawrence streets. The 99-unit nature of the filing means Klein will likely try to utilize the city’s controversial 485-x tax abatement program, which comes with a construction wage requirement for projects with 100 or more units. Klein’s proposal calls for a 99-unit, 27-story building at 485 Fulton Street. The registered architect is Kao Hwa Lee from Kao Hwa Lee Architects. Neither the architect nor the developer responded to Commercial Observer’s requests for comment. If approved, the building at 485 Fulton Street would have between four and eight residential units across the third through 27th floors. There would also be commercial and community facility space, as well as nearly 3,000 square feet of outdoor rooftop space for tenants. There are no further amenity details, but offerings including workout space, communal lounges, and coworking options have become non-negotiables in new residential developments. The other two 99-unit buildings would be built at 147 and 149 Lawrence Street, with similar makeups, according to the filing. The tenants of Klein’s new project would have a plethora of entertainment options in the neighborhood. The building is located across the street from 422 Fulton Street, a former Macy’s department store, which is being renovated into a five-floor retail and entertainment spot called BKX, CO previously reported. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Shimon Klein filed plans for 297 residential units across three 99-unit buildings, Downtown Brooklyn, Fulton Street.
Project at 485 Fulton Street: 27-story tower with 99 units; Klein likely pursuing 485-x tax abatement to avoid wage requirements.
Positioned directly across from Macy's retail redevelopment; targeted commercial/community facility space plus 3K SF rooftop.
stories.summary: Local developer Shimon Klein filed Department of Buildings applications for three separate 99-unit residential towers totaling 297 units along Fulton Street in Downtown Brooklyn, between Bridge and Lawrence streets. The lead property at 485 Fulton would be a 27-story building configured to exploit the city's 485-x tax abatement program, which avoids prevailing wage requirements for projects under 100 units. The site sits directly across from the Macy's retail redevelopment and includes commercial/community facility space.
stories.impact: Klein's filing structure signals developer strategy to avoid NYC prevailing wage thresholds—a key cost lever for feasibility in expensive Brooklyn markets. Clustering 99-unit buildings suggests builder expects strong demand and rent growth justified by proximity to Macy's retail anchor and Fulton Street's transit hub. Tax abatement arbitrage and phased delivery can improve IRRs; success here will validate Downtown Brooklyn's ability to absorb new luxury/middle-market supply post-pandemic, reinforcing capital competition for infill sites in the borough.

stories.title: Wind Energy Supplier Inks Lease at Brookshire Industrial Park
stories.excerpt: Vestas-American Wind Technology leased approximately 131,300 square feet of space at Enterprise Park at Twinwood in Brookshire, Texas. The Class A industrial warehouse and office facility sits on approximately 17 acres and will support Vestas’ spare parts distribution and operations across North America. JLL’s Louis Rosenthal, Graham Horton, Cayla Wardenburg and Eric Turner represented Vestas-American Wind Technology in the transaction. Bill Gold and Faron Wiley of CBRE represented the landlord, Twinwood Industrial Owner LLC. Vestas-American Wind Technology is the North American division of Vestas, a leading provider of sustainable energy solutions and one of the world’s largest wind turbine manufacturers. The company designs, manufactures, installs and services wind energy systems. The new Brookshire facility will strengthen Vestas’ spare parts distribution network, allowing the company to better support its growing wind turbine distribution to meet demand for customers throughout the region. The post Wind Energy Supplier Inks Lease at Brookshire Industrial Park appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Vestas-American Wind Technology leased 131,300 SF at Enterprise Park at Twinwood, Brookshire, Texas.
Facility supports spare parts distribution and North American operations for global wind turbine manufacturer.
Class A industrial warehouse on 17 acres strengthens Vestas' supply-chain footprint near Houston market.
stories.summary: Vestas-American Wind Technology, the North American division of global wind turbine manufacturer Vestas, leased approximately 131,300 square feet of Class A industrial warehouse and office space at Enterprise Park at Twinwood in Brookshire, Texas. The facility will serve as a spare parts distribution and operations hub to support growing wind turbine demand across the region. JLL and CBRE represented both tenant and landlord.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact, but Vestas' regional HQ and distribution expansion signals energy-sector job growth in Greater Houston; manufacturing and supply-chain employment typically drives housing demand among middle-income workers. Industrial growth in Brookshire corridor may attract speculative multifamily development in nearby submarkets (Tomball, Magnolia) where commute times remain reasonable and affordable rental stock is limited—creating long-term demand tailwinds for outland infill and new-build communities.

stories.title: Avelo Airlines Reveals First McKinney National Airport Flights
stories.excerpt: McKinney National Airport’s new $79 million commercial passenger terminal is on track to start hosting flights starting in November. Avelo Airlines will launch the first-ever commercial passenger service at McKinney National Airport (DTX) on November 11, 2026. The low-cost carrier is establishing a local base with two Boeing 737 aircraft, offering nonstop flights to Las Vegas and four Florida destinations. The facility includes a 45,000-square-foot terminal with four initial gates, expanded vehicle parking, and upgraded ramp/taxiway infrastructure. Construction of the commercial terminal began in 2025. McKinney will be the third commercial airport in the DFW, along with Dallas Fort Worth International Airport and Dallas Love Field. Avelo Airlines, Inc. is an American ultra-low-cost airline headquartered in Houston, Texas. It previously operated charter flights as Casino Express Airlines and Xtra Airways before transitioning to scheduled operations and rebranding as Avelo Airlines on April 8, 2021. The post Avelo Airlines Reveals First McKinney National Airport Flights appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Avelo Airlines launches first commercial service at McKinney National Airport on November 11, 2026.
New $79M, 45,000 SF terminal with four gates; Avelo basing two Boeing 737s with flights to Las Vegas and four Florida cities.
McKinney becomes third commercial airport in DFW; terminal construction began 2025.
stories.summary: McKinney National Airport's new $79 million commercial passenger terminal will open with Avelo Airlines service beginning November 11, 2026. The ultra-low-cost carrier is establishing a local base with two Boeing 737 aircraft, offering nonstop flights to Las Vegas and four Florida destinations. The 45,000-square-foot facility includes four initial gates, expanded parking, and improved ramp/taxiway infrastructure. McKinney will become the third commercial airport serving the Dallas-Fort Worth metropolitan area.
stories.impact: New low-cost carrier service expands airport access for North Dallas residents and businesses, reducing friction for leisure and business travel. This can accelerate residential demand in McKinney and surrounding Collin County submarkets by attracting relocating professionals and expanding corporate footprints; improved air connectivity historically boosts multifamily lease-up velocity and rent growth in previously car-dependent exurban markets. Developer should monitor Avelo route expansion and corporate tenant recruitment around DTX to identify emerging demand nodes for acquisition or development.

stories.title: Spirit Airlines Dania Beach HQ Sells at Auction for $93.25M
stories.excerpt: Spirit Airlines’ shuttered headquarters building in Dania Beach was acquired at auction for $93.25 million. A Hill City Capital affiliate was the buyer of the office campus, totaling over 600,000 square feet. The facility was delivered just two years ago. The campus covered more than 11 acres and comprised four buildings, including corporate offices, an amenity building, a crew-training facility with flight simulators and corporate housing. The low-cost carrier shut down abruptly on May 2 after a last-minute bailout from the federal government failed to materialize. About 17,000 employees lost their jobs. With the airline no longer operating, its bankruptcy estate began monetizing its remaining assets. That includes aircraft, equipment, airport-related assets and real estate. Hill City Capital is a Boston-based investment firm and hedge fund founded in 2020. It manages roughly $4.9 billion in discretionary assets focusing on concentrated, long-biased equity strategies within sectors like industrials, transportation, and business services The post Spirit Airlines Dania Beach HQ Sells at Auction for $93.25M appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Spirit Airlines headquarters campus in Dania Beach, Florida sold at auction for $93.25M to Hill City Capital affiliate.
600,000+ SF, 11-acre campus with four buildings (offices, crew training, corporate housing) delivered just two years prior.
Spirit ceased operations May 2, 2024; bankruptcy estate monetizing assets including real estate.
stories.summary: Spirit Airlines' headquarters campus in Dania Beach, Florida—comprising over 600,000 square feet across four buildings on 11 acres—was acquired at auction by a Hill City Capital affiliate for $93.25 million. The newly delivered facility included corporate offices, amenity building, crew-training facility with flight simulators, and corporate housing. Spirit shut down abruptly on May 2, 2024, after a federal bailout failed, idling 17,000 employees and triggering bankruptcy asset monetization.
stories.impact: Massive office/industrial asset in South Florida real estate market now in distressed liquidation; Hill City's acquisition suggests repositioning intent (e.g., industrial conversion, logistics, or spec office sublease). Sudden loss of 17,000 jobs in Broward/Miami-Dade creates near-term headwind for residential leasing velocity and rent growth, as displaced workers reduce new household formation and household income. However, distressed asset sales often presage value-add opportunities; monitor if Hill City converts or redevelops the campus, which could stabilize regional employment and support medium-term multifamily absorption in Dania Beach and west Broward submarkets.

stories.title: Payments Manager Corpay Cross-Border Relocates to 18K SF at 560 Lexington Avenue
stories.excerpt: An international payment and currency risk management firm is planning a headquarters relocation to Rudin’s 560 Lexington Avenue. Corpay Cross-Border Solutions, which operates under corporate payments company Corpay, has signed an 11-year lease for 17,778 square feet at the Plaza District tower, Commercial Observer has learned. The landlord declined to provide the asking rent, but an April lease inside Rudin’s 22-story tower asked $84 per square foot, according to previous CO reports. Jacob Rosenthal and Kevin Carroll of CBRE represented Corpay, while Rudin was represented in-house by Kevin Daly and a CBRE team of Peter Turchin, Brett Shannon, Eric Deutsch and Lauren Levy. Corpay Cross-Border plans to move from Tishman Speyer‘s 300 Park Avenue into its new, prebuilt office, which occupies the entire 17th floor of 560 Lexington, this fall. Daly, Rudin’s vice president of office leasing, stated that the deal validates recent portfolio investments, which allowed for minimal modifications to meet Corpay’s space requirements. “This allowed us to accommodate their accelerated timeline for move-in, which was a big factor in getting the deal done,” Daly said. Located two blocks from Grand Central Terminal, the 380,000-square-foot office building at the corner of Lexington Avenue and East 50th Street has seen over 91,000 square feet of leasing activity in the last six months, according to Rudin. Recent arrivals include financial firm Marex, hedge fund SummitTX and coworking firm Industrious. Spokespeople for CBRE and Corpay Cross-Border did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Corpay Cross-Border Solutions signed 11-year lease for 17,778 SF at Rudin's 560 Lexington Avenue, Manhattan.
Company relocating headquarters from Tishman Speyer's 300 Park Avenue; move-in fall 2025.
Recent comps at 560 Lexington at $84/SF; tenant occupies full 17th floor with prebuilt office.
stories.summary: Corpay Cross-Border Solutions, an international payment and currency risk management firm, leased 17,778 square feet at Rudin's 560 Lexington Avenue (Plaza District, Manhattan) for 11 years. The company is relocating headquarters from Tishman Speyer's 300 Park Avenue and will occupy the entire 17th floor with prebuilt office. Comparable asking rents at the building were recently $84 per square foot; tenant plans occupancy in fall 2025.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily signal, but Corpay's Midtown lease renewal and tower selection reflects stabilization of Manhattan's Class A office market and return of corporate tenancy confidence. Successful pre-built office and rapid lease-up at Plaza District validates Rudin's strategy; sustained office tenant morale and occupancy can support adjacent and nearby multifamily by maintaining CBD employment base and worker commuting patterns. However, office-to-residential conversion remains a longer-term alternative if office demand falters again.

stories.title: John McCullough of Kennedy Wilson Multifamily Development: 5 Questions
stories.excerpt: Since joining Kennedy Wilson following the firm’s $347 million acquisition of Toll Brothers’ apartment living platform in 2025, John McCullough has been serving as president of the real estate investment company’s multifamily development group, where he oversees every aspect of the firm’s U.S. development business. Kennedy Wilson’s acquisition of Toll Brothers’ platform gave it general partner interests in 18 apartment and student housing properties, with assets under management of $2.2 billion. The firm also purchased a pipeline of 29 development sites in various stages of construction. Toll Brothers’ entire apartment living management team has transitioned over to Kennedy Wilson under the leadership of McCullough, who previously led apartment living operations at Toll Brothers. But McCullough’s real estate path wasn’t always laid out for him, as he started out in the U.S. Navy and then eventually hit his business stride at school in Boston. Commercial Observer caught up with McCullough last month to discuss his entry into real estate, the Toll Brothers acquisition, and his mission at Kennedy Wilson. This conversation has been edited for length and clarity. Commercial Observer: How’d you get started in real estate? John McCullough: I got started in real estate in a roundabout way. I went to the United States Naval Academy for my undergrad, and graduated in 1994, and then served five years in what we would refer to as the surface navy. If I had stayed in the Navy long-term, I would have trained to be the captain of a ship. I served on two large aircraft carriers out in San Diego, and it was a great experience. It was a really good grounding in the fundamentals of leadership I was put into a lot of situations that were incredibly difficult as a 23- or 24-year-old, but I learned a lot from that. bullets: Kennedy Wilson acquired Toll Brothers apartment living platform for $347M in 2025; McCullough named president of multifamily development.
Acquisition includes GP interests in 18 apartment/student housing properties ($2.2B AUM) and 29-site development pipeline.
Toll Brothers' entire apartment management team transitioned under McCullough's leadership.
stories.summary: Kennedy Wilson completed a $347 million acquisition of Toll Brothers' apartment living platform in 2025, with John McCullough appointed president of the firm's multifamily development group. The deal includes general partner interests in 18 apartment and student housing properties with $2.2 billion in assets under management, plus a pipeline of 29 development sites in various stages of construction. Toll Brothers' entire apartment management team transitioned to Kennedy Wilson under McCullough's leadership.
stories.impact: Significant industry consolidation signal: major institutional platform acquisition indicates capital appetite and confidence in multifamily fundamentals despite rate uncertainty in late 2024–early 2025. Kennedy Wilson's integration of Toll Brothers' 29-site pipeline accelerates delivery into tight markets; new ownership/operator transitions often unlock value through cost reduction and capital redeployment. Monitor McCullough's development strategy and site dispositions—pipeline rationalization and strategic redirection could reshape competitive dynamics in core markets and signal where institutional capital expects strongest returns in next 2–3 years.
